source_text: Φησὶν οὖν· τὰ μὲν ὑπὸ τῆς Πυθίας ἢ Δωδωνίδων ἢ Κλαρίου ἢ ἐν Βραγχίδαις ἢ ἐν Ἄμμωνος ὑπὸ μυρίων τε ἄλλων θεοπρόπων προειρημένα, ὑφ᾿ ὧν ἐπιεικῶς πᾶσα γῆ κατῳκίσθη, ταῦτα μὲν (ἐν) οὐδενὶ λόγῳ τίθενται· τὰ δὲ ὑπο τῶν ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ τῷ ἐκείνων τρόπῳ λεχθέντα ἢ μὴ λεχθέντα, καὶ ὥσπερ εἰώθασιν ἔτι νῦν οἱ περὶ Φοινίκην τε καὶ Παλαιστίνην, ταῦτά γε θαυμαστὰ καὶ ἀπαράλλακτα ἡγοῦνται. λέγωμεν οὖν περὶ τῶν κατειλεγμένων χρηστηρίων ὅτι δυνατὸν μὲν ἡμῖν συνάγουσιν ἀπὸ Ἀριστοτέλους καὶ τῶν τὰ τοῦ Περιπάτου φιλοσοφησάντων οὐκ ὀλίγα εἰπεῖν εἰς ἀνατροπὴν τοῦ περὶ τῆς Πυθίας καὶ τῶν λοιπῶν χρηστηρίων λόγου· δυνατὸν δὲ καὶ τὰ λελεγμένα τῷ Ἐπικούρῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀσπαζομένοις αὐτοῦ τὸν λόγον περὶ τῶν αὐτῶν παραθέμενον δεῖξαι ὅτι καὶ Ἑλλήνων τινὲς ἀνατρέπουσι τὰς νομιζομένας καὶ τεθαυμασμένας ἐν πάσῃ Ἑλλάδι θεοπροπίας. ἀλλὰ γὰρ δεδόσθω μὴ εἶναι πλάσματα μηδὲ προσποιήσεις ἀνθρώπων περὶ θεοφορίας τὰ περὶ τὴν Πυθίαν καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ χρηστήρια· ἴδωμεν οὖν εἰ μὴ καὶ οὕτως δύναται τοῖς φιλαλήθως ἐξετάζουσι τὰ πράγματα ἀποδείκνυσθαι ὅτι καὶ τῷ παραδεχομένῳ εἶναι ταῦτα τὰ μαντεῖα οὐκ ἀναγκαῖον προσέσθαι ὅτι θεοί τινες εἰσὶ παρ᾿ αὐτοῖς, ἀλλ᾿ ἐκ τοῦ ἐναντίου δαίμονές τινες φαῦλοι καὶ πνεύματα ἐχθρὰ τῷ γένει τῶν ἀνθρώπων καὶ κωλύοντα τὴν τῆς ψυχῆς ἄνοδον καὶ δι᾿ ἀρετῆς πορείαν καὶ τῆς ἀληθινῆς εὐσεβείας ἀποκατάστασιν πρὸς τὸν θεόν. ἱστόρηται τοίνυν περὶ τῆς Πυθίας, ὅπερ δοκεῖ τῶν ἄλλων μαντείων λαμπρότερον τυγχάνειν. ὅτι περικαθεζομένη τὸ τῆς Κασταλίας στόμιον ἡ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος προφῆτις δέχεται πνεῦμα διὰ τῶν γυναικείων κόλπων· οὗ πληρωθεῖσα ἀποφθέγγεται τὰ νομιζόμενα εἶναι σεμνὰ καὶ θεῖα μαντεύματα. ὅρα δὴ διὰ τούτων εἰ μὴ τὸ τοῦ πνεύματος ἐκείνου ἀκάθαρτον καὶ βέβηλον ἐμφαίνεται, μὴ διὰ μανῶν καὶ ἀφανῶν πόρων καὶ πολλῷ γυναικείων κόλπων καθαρωτέρων ἐπεισιὸν τῇ ψυχῇ τῆς θεσπιζούσης ἀλλὰ διὰ τούτων, ἃ οὐδὲ θέμις ἦν τῷ σώφρονι καὶ ἀνθρώπῳ βλέπειν, οὔπω λέγεσθαι ἢ καὶ ἅπτεσθαι· καὶ τοῦτο ποιεῖν οὐχ ἅπαξ που οὐδὲ δὶς (ἴσως γὰρ ἔδοξεν ἀνεκτότερον τὸ τοιοῦτο τυγχάνειν), ἀλλὰ τοσαυτάκις, ὁσάκις προφητεύειν ἐκείνη ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἀπόλλωνος πεπίστευται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸ εἰς ἔκστασιν καὶ μανικὴν ἄγειν κατάστασιν τὴν δῆθεν προφητεύουσαν, ὡς μηδαμῶς αυτὴν ἑαυτῇ παρακολουθεῖν, οὐ θείου πνεύματος ἔργον ἐστίν· ἐχρῆν γὰρ τὸν κάτοχον τῷ θείῳ πνεύματι πολλῷ πρότερον παντὸς οὑτινοσοῦν τοῦ ἀπὸ τῶν χρησμῶν διδασκομένου τὸ συμβαλλόμενον εἰς τὸν μέσον καὶ κατὰ φύσιν βίον ἢ πρὸς τὸ λυσιτελὲς ἢ πρὸς τὸ συμφέρον ὠφεληθῆναι καὶ διορατικώτερον παρ᾿ ἐκεῖνο μάλιστα καιροῦ τυγχάνειν, ὅτε σύνεστιν αὐτῷ τὸ θεῖον.
pass_a_gloss: He says then: the things spoken by the Pythia or the Dodonian or the Clarian or in Branchidae or in Ammon by thousands of other prophets, by whom the whole earth was inhabited in a gentle manner, these things are not considered in any word; but the things spoken by those in Judea in their manner, or not spoken, and as those around Phoenicia and Palestine are accustomed even now, these things they consider wonderful and unwavering. Let us say then concerning the oracles that have been spoken that it is possible for us to gather from Aristotle and those who philosophized in the Peripatetic manner not a few things to overturn the word concerning the Pythia and the other oracles; it is possible also to show the things said by Epicurus and those who welcome his word concerning the same things, that some Greeks also overturn the divinations believed and marveled at in all of Greece. But if it is granted that they are not fabrications nor human pretenses concerning divine inspiration, the things concerning the Pythia and the other oracles, let us see if it is possible to demonstrate to those who examine things in a love of truth that even if one accepts that these are oracles, it is not necessary to agree that some gods are present, but rather that they are evil demons and hostile spirits to the human race, hindering the ascent of the soul and the journey through virtue and the restoration of true piety towards God. It is reported then concerning the Pythia, which seems to be more renowned than the other oracles, that sitting around the mouth of Castalia, the prophetess of Apollo receives a spirit through the female organs; having been filled with this, she utters the things considered to be solemn and divine prophecies. See then through these things if the spirit's impurity and profanity are not revealed, not entering the soul of the prophetess through pure and invisible sources, but through those things which it was not even lawful for a sane and human person to see or touch; and this is done not once or twice (for perhaps such a thing seemed more tolerable), but as many times as she is believed to prophesy from Apollo. But also the fact that it leads the supposed prophetess to a state of ecstasy and madness, so that she is not following herself, is not the work of a divine spirit; for the one possessed by the divine spirit ought to have been benefited much earlier by all that is taught from the oracles, concerning the middle and natural life, either for what is useful or for what is advantageous, and to have been more discerning, especially at the time when the divine is present to him.
pass_b_english: He goes on to say that the pronouncements once delivered by the Pythia, the Dodonian priests, the Clarian oracle, the shrine at Branchidae, the oracle of Ammon, and by countless other prophets — prophets through whom the whole earth was settled in a gentle way — are not even taken into account. Yet the utterances of those in Judea, whether spoken in the same manner or not, and the sort of thing still customary among the peoples around Phoenicia and Palestine, these are treated as wonderfully reliable and unchangeable. Let us therefore speak about the oracles that have been handed down. It is possible for us to collect from Aristotle and from those who philosophized in the Peripatetic tradition no small number of arguments to overturn the case for the Pythia and the other oracles. It is also possible to cite the words of Epicurus and of those who embrace his teaching on the same matters, and to show that some Greeks themselves reject the divinations believed and marveled at throughout all Greece. But let us grant that the matters concerning the Pythia and the other oracles are neither fabrications nor human pretenses about divine inspiration. Even so, let us see whether it can be demonstrated to those who examine things in a love of truth that, even if one accepts these as genuine oracles, it is not necessary to conclude that gods are present in them. Rather, they are evil demons and hostile spirits, enemies of the human race, who hinder the soul's ascent and the journey through virtue and the restoration of true piety toward God. Now, it is reported about the Pythia — who appears to be the most renowned of the other oracles — that the prophetess of Apollo, sitting over the mouth of the Castalian spring, receives a spirit through the female organs; and when she has been filled with it, she utters the things regarded as solemn and divine prophecies. Observe, then, through these facts whether the impurity and profanity of that spirit are not revealed. It does not enter the soul of the prophetess through pure and invisible channels, but through those parts which it was not even lawful for a sane and human person to see, let alone touch. And this is done not merely once or twice — for perhaps such a thing might seem more tolerable — but as many times as she is believed to prophesy from Apollo. Moreover, the fact that it drives the supposed prophetess into a state of ecstasy and madness, so that she does not follow herself, is not the work of a divine spirit. For the one possessed by the divine spirit ought to have been benefited far earlier by all that is taught from the oracles concerning the middle and natural life — whether for what is useful or for what is advantageous — and ought to be more discerning, especially at the very time when the divine is present to him.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the complex conditional structures and the specific theological distinctions regarding the nature of the spirits (demons vs. gods). Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
